Hi Samir - quick technical notes to help your engineers choose a path. Short answers first: for speed of POC we recommend keeping candidate gen in FAISS and calling our rerank endpoint per-query with batched candidates. Bulk scoring is supported if you prefer fewer network hops.

Python quickstart (example):

pip install redwood-sdk
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")

# basic rerank call
response = client.rerank.run(query="how to reset password", candidates=[{"id":"doc1","text":"..."}, {"id":"doc2","text":"..."}], rerank_k=20)

Notes:
- Request shape supports candidate ids, text, or embeddings. We return structured output with scores and optional per-candidate metadata.
- Tune retrieval_k and rerank_k per the sweep plan. Recommended defaults in the attached eval_sweep_plan.md.
- For high throughput you can batch multiple queries; we find batch sizes 8-32 work well on GPU-backed endpoints.

I'll drop a dockerized test harness in the shared Drive that runs the sweep and emits MRR/NDCG CSVs if that helps.

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
